Harrodsburg, Kentucky · welcoming travelers since 1919

Sleep inside 180 years of Kentucky history.

Kentucky's oldest family inn: four-poster beds under 1845 ceilings, a James Beard–recognized kitchen, and a bourbon bar with more than a hundred bottles — all a short drive from Shaker Village, the Bourbon Trail, and Lexington's autumn race days.

The rooms

No two rooms alike. Every one of them slept in for a century.

Thirty-plus guest rooms across the main inn and its historic outbuildings, each furnished with antiques, period wallpapers, and beds you'll write home about. Modern baths, quiet nights, and a porch never far away.

Rooms with a past

Striped and floral papers, marble-top dressers, and chandeliers that were hung when the building was a college. Nothing here was bought to look old; it is old, and cared for.

Vintage outside, modern where it counts

Rope-twist bedposts and a mantel, then a private bath, a deep mattress, crisp white linens, climate control, and Wi-Fi. The romance of 1845 with none of its inconveniences.

Room to settle in

Wingback chairs at a marble table, twin windows, and a bed with posts nearly to the ceiling. Quiet enough to sleep late, comfortable enough to stay another night.

A short history

More than an Inn.

Most hotels are built to be hotels. This one was built to be a school for young women, and it became an inn only because one alumna refused to let it disappear.

The walls remember.

The brick building under the columns went up in 1845 as Greenville Institute, and for the next seventy years it educated the daughters of Kentucky as Daughters' College and then Beaumont College, one of the few full-curriculum colleges for women in the state.

When the college closed, a former student and teacher, Annie Bell Goddard, bought the campus back and opened it as an inn in 1919. Franklin D. Roosevelt sat in the parlor. The recipes on tonight's menu were written down by hand generations ago.

In 2015 the James Beard Foundation named Beaumont Inn an America's Classic, an award given to restaurants with timeless appeal, beloved in their region for quality food that reflects the character of their community.

Harrodsburg & beyond

The oldest town in Kentucky, in the middle of everything worth driving to.

Harrodsburg sits between horse country and bourbon country. Make the inn your base and let the day trips come to you.

  • Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill3,000 acres of restored Shaker buildings, trails, and river boat rides.

Dining at the inn

A James Beard kitchen, a bourbon bar, and a Friday the whole county circles.

The recipes that made the inn famous, still made the same way: yellow-legged fried chicken, Kentucky cured ham, corn pudding, and the cakes guests drive hours for. Beside them, a new chapter: seasonal dishes from a kitchen that honors the legacy on every plate while writing the next page of it.

Main Dining Room

Breakfast Wednesday–Sunday · Bi-weekly Friday lunch buffet · Sunday brunch periodically

The heart of the inn since 1919. Country ham, fried chicken, corn pudding, and the cakes that earned a James Beard America's Classic award, served in the rooms where the college once dined.

Old Owl Tavern & Owl's Nest

Evenings · 100+ Kentucky bourbons · dinner, cocktails & lounge

Downstairs, low-lit, with the deepest bourbon shelf for miles. Flights and rare pours, a tavern menu built for after a day on the trail, and the Owl's Nest lounge for a cocktail, a sandwich, or the game if you want it.

The Friday Buffet

every other Friday · guests eat first

Twice a month the dining room sets out the full spread: fried chicken, cured ham, hot browns, corn pudding, biscuits, and the dessert table. Locals plan their week around it. Guests staying with us on a buffet Friday simply walk downstairs.

Match your dates to a buffet Friday and you'll understand why people call it worth the drive.

Before you book

The questions guests ask us most.

Is breakfast really included?

Yes. Overnight guests receive a complimentary breakfast Wednesday through Sunday. On Monday and Tuesday we'll point you to our favorite spot in town.

How far are you from Lexington and the race track?

Harrodsburg is roughly 35 miles southwest of Lexington. Plan on about 45 minutes to the track on a race day, and a quiet, dark drive home after.

Which Fridays are buffet Fridays?

The buffet runs every other Friday. Check the dates on our dining page before you pick your nights, or call the front desk and we'll match your stay to one.

Are the rooms historic on the inside too?

The furnishings are antiques from the family collection, and the wallpapers and beds are period. Every room has a private bath, climate control, Wi-Fi, and a television.

Do you host groups, rehearsal dinners, or weddings?

Yes. With 30+ rooms across the campus and three dining spaces, we host wedding weekends, rehearsal dinners, family reunions, and corporate retreats. Ask about blocking rooms.

Is there parking?

Complimentary on-site parking for guests, steps from every building.

What is the cancellation policy?

[Confirm before launch] Reservations may be cancelled without charge up to 48 hours before arrival. Special event and race weekends may carry a longer window; it's shown before you confirm.

Can I bring my dog, or my kids?

[Confirm before launch] Children are welcome throughout the inn. We're not able to accommodate pets in the guest rooms, but we're happy to recommend a local kennel.
